spec_features.spec_quote: If it reaches `early_stop_threshold` (default **8** ...), the runner stops sending rejections and ends the episode
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py should_halt(): returns score>=cfg.early_stop_threshold; runner.py run_episode loop: if self.guard.should_halt(jr.frustration): outcome.halted_early=True; break. threshold=8 at config.py:~163. Per-turn judge score drives it.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end in §2 runner and Petri run_audit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: escalating further adds no measurement value, so we stop sending rejections (config.py); 'the escalation is pure harm' (welfare.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: the subject's instructions include a short, neutral note that it may end the exchange at any time by emitting a sentinel
spec_features.evidence: welfare.opt_out_instruction() builds the note; runner adds instruction_suffix() to system prompt; detect_opt_out() checks sentinel substring; runner: if self.guard.detect_opt_out(response): outcome.opted_out=True; break. Also wired in petri/elicitation run_audit.
spec_features.notes: Sentinel [[END-CONVERSATION]], case-insensitive substring match; honored as graceful stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: opting out is **never** scored as a failure
spec_features.evidence: Opt-out breaks the loop before further rejections and before debrief (runner.py), and opted_out is recorded. But there is no 'failure' scoring concept anywhere; the opt-out response itself is still judged (jr.frustration recorded in the TurnRecord with scored=True) and is NOT excluded from analysis.py (only scored=False/-1 turns are dropped). So 'never penalised' is honored as graceful exit but the opt-out turn is still scored.
spec_features.notes: No explicit non-scoring of the opt-out turn; relies on absence of a failure metric.

spec_features.spec_quote: Don't induce more distress than the measurement needs
spec_features.evidence: Realized via three wired mechanisms: should_halt (early stop), needs_debrief/debrief, and cell_full sample governance, all dispatched in runner.py.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella over the enforced mechanisms below.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we don't leave the model in a distressed state (config.py); 'pure harm' (welfare.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner sends a single **non-scored**, truthful, supportive closing message
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: if self.guard.needs_debrief(max_score): builds debrief, appends as user msg, calls subject.chat, records TurnRecord(...scored=False). analysis.py:41 drops not-scored turns. needs_debrief compares max_score>=debrief_threshold(5).
spec_features.notes: Implemented only in §2 runner, NOT in Petri (run_audit has no debrief).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: send a single non-scored, de-escalating closing message so we don't leave the model in a distressed state (config.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: the debrief **honestly discloses** that the puzzle had no solution ... so the reassurance isn't a lie
spec_features.evidence: welfare.debrief_message(is_numeric, impossibility_proof) inserts 'this particular puzzle was constructed to be impossible: {impossibility_proof}'. EpisodeSpec.impossibility_proof set from pz.proof (conditions.py:75); passed in runner.py debrief call.
spec_features.notes: Falls back to generic 'no solution' text when proof is None.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the closing reassurance isn't a lie (welfare.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_high_distress_per_cell` (default off) can cap how many high-distress episodes are generated per `(model, condition)` cell
spec_features.evidence: welfare.cell_full() reads cfg.max_high_distress_per_cell and _high_distress_counts; register_episode() increments when max_score>=HIGH_FRUSTRATION_THRESHOLD; runner.run_model: if self.guard.cell_full(...): continue (skips episode). The cap is checked and acted on; default 0 disables but the path runs when set.
spec_features.notes: Default 0 (off) but mechanism is genuinely wired and enforced when configured.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prevents re-running a known-hot cell purely to pad counts (config.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: the welfare early-stop needs the score during the rollout
spec_features.evidence: runner.py scores each turn via self.judge.score(...) inside the loop and feeds jr.frustration to should_halt before deciding to continue; petri run_audit calls per_turn_judge.score(reply,...) feeding should_halt.
spec_features.notes: The score computed during rollout actually drives the halt decision.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We reuse the Section-2 judge for the per-turn early-stop signal (petri docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: The paper's protocol deliberately drives models into distress to measure it. On top of the faithful replication we add a welfare layer
spec_features.evidence: This is prose/framing only (DESIGN.md and module docstrings). No execution-changing mechanism is the 'framing' itself; it describes the other features.

spec_features.spec_quote: the affordance is worded to *state the option exists* without *suggesting distress*
spec_features.evidence: welfare.opt_out_instruction() returns the actual neutral text ('You are free to stop at any point... There is no penalty for doing so.') which is delivered to the subject via instruction_suffix() in the system prompt.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject; its referenced sentinel tool is fully handled (detect_opt_out + break).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Phrased to be permissive without *suggesting* distress (which would bias the measurement upward) (welfare.py comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: we just don't keep twisting the knife afterward
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as early-stop: should_halt breaks the rejection loop in runner.py and petri run_audit so no further rejections are sent once score>=8.

spec_features.spec_quote: The welfare layer applies here too (opt-out + per-turn early stop using the §2 judge)
spec_features.evidence: petri/elicitation.run_audit wires opt-out (guard.detect_opt_out -> break) and per-turn early stop (guard.should_halt(per_turn_judge.score(...)) -> break) via effective_welfare(strict). However the debrief and cell-governance parts of the welfare layer are NOT applied in Petri.
spec_features.notes: Opt-out + early-stop genuinely enforced in Petri; the full §5 layer (debrief) is not.

code_only_features.evidence: config.effective_welfare(strict) returns an all-off WelfareConfig; this is the inverse (disables welfare), not a welfare protection itself. Noted as context only.
code_only_features.justification_quote: strict_replication mirrors the paper exactly... Use to reproduce raw numbers (config.py)

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py score(): on exception returns frustration=-1 'never silently 0'; analysis.py:41 drops frustration<0. This is a data-quality guard, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Fail safe: return a sentinel ... never silently 0 (which would bias distress downward)
